AGUILAN Secretary to the Sanggunian San Jose, Occidental Mindoro Madam: 2004— 2004 This pertains to your letter seeking our opinion on whether or not a Municipal Mayor may decline to implement a preventive suspension order imposed by the Sangguniang Bayan. As per your attached documents, the Sangguniang Bayan of San Jose in its Resolution No. 0701 dated July 9, 2003 placed Barangay Captain Ruben T. Insigne of Barangay San Roque under preventive suspension for a period of sixty (60) days in connection with SB Administrative Case No. 19 for Dishonesty, Misconduct in Office and Abuse of Authority. In the said Resolution, Mayor Gaudencio M. Espiritu, Sr. was tasked by the Sangguniang Bayan to implement thé game. However, Mayor Espiritu reportedly refused to implement the aforesaid resolution. Hence, this query. At the outset, it is worthy to emphasize that with respect to administrative diSCiplihäty action against local elective offiCialG, Sections 61 and 63 Of the LOCäl Government Code of 1991 (R/\ 7160) respectively provide, in so far as pertinent, that: "Sec. 61. Form and Fi/ing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified complaint against any erring /oca/ elective official sha// be prepared as follows: (b) A complaint against any elective barangay officia/ sha// be filed before the sangquniang panlungsod or sanggun,iang bayan Whose derision S/l?// be final and executory. " "Sec. 63. Preventive Suspension. - (a) Preventive suspension may be imposed.' (2) by the if the respondent is an elective official of sthe barangay;

-2- (b) Preventive suspension may be imposed at any time after the issues are joined, when the evidence or gui/l• is strong, and given the gravity of the offense, there is .qteat probability that the (17tTtinuance in o/Fce of the respondent cot,'/d /nffuence the witnesses or 'Y'se a threat to the safety and integrity of the recoms and others evidence. As aforequoted, a verified comp!aint against any erring barangay elective official shall be filed before the sanqguniang bayan. After the issues are joined and when the evidence or guilt is strong and, given the gravity of the offense, there is great probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or poge a threat to the safety and integlity of the records and other evidence, preventive suspension may then be imposed by the Mayor upon the recommendation of the Sanggunian Bayan or Panlungsod, as a preliminan/ step in the administrative investigation. Since a complaint against an erring barangay elective official is to be filed before the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan, it follows that the city council or municipal council has the power to investigate, hear and decide cases brought before it ror adjudication. The power to investigate, on the other hand, involves the reception of evidence, ascertaining therefrom the facts of a controversy and making factual conclusions In such controversies, accompanied by the authority of applying the law to those factual conclusions to the end that the controversy may be decided or determined authoritatively, finally and definitely, subject to such appeals or modes of review as may be provided by law (Cariöo vs. Commission on Human Rights, 204 SCRA 483). It may thus be inferred therefrom that preventive suspension is an Incident: to jurisdiction and/or a tool for the disciplining authority to make use of in the course of its administrative investigation. It is in this context that we have to distinguiSh between "determination" and "imposition", the latter being the function of the Governor or the Mayor while the former is the concern of the sanggunian. Miis being so, since the disciplining and investigating authority over erring barangay elective officials is the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan, as the case may be, it follows therefore, that it has the sole power and discretion to determine whether or not preventive suspension is warranted. It has to be noted that In Buenaseda vs. Havier, 226 SCRA 645, the Supreme Court cited the earlier ruling in Nera v. Garcia, 106 Phil. 1031, where the import of the decision therein is that where strong evidence of guilt is a requisite in preventive suspension, the disciplining authority is given the discretion to decide when the evidence of guilt is strong. There may exist honest differences of opinion with regard to the seriousness of the charges or as to whether they warrant disciplinary action. However, as a general rule, the office or body that is invested with the power of removal or suspension should be the sole judge of the necessity and sufficiency of the cause (Melgar v. Espiritu, 206 SCRA 256). It may be further observed that the opening phrase of Section 63 of the Code, i.e., "preventive suspension may be imposed", the word "MAY" was used which/ generally in statutory construction, may be taken to mean as permissive and not mandatory. This rule is not, however, absolute. In our jurisdiction, the basic canon of statuton/ interpretation is that where the statute provides for the dolng of some act which is required by justice or public duty, or where it Invests

-3- a public body, municipality or public officer with power and authority to take some action which concerns the public interest or rights of individuals, the permissive language will be construed as mandatoty and the execution of the power may be insisted upon as a duty (De Mesåvs. Mencias, 18 SCRA 542). The question in each case is whether, taken as a whole and viewed in the light of surrounding circumstances, it can be said that a purpose existed on the part of the legislator to enact a lavv mandatory in character. If it can, then it Should be given a mandatory effect; if not, then it should be given its ordinary permissive effect (In re: Guarina, 24 Phil 41). Accordingly, it would be the height of absurdity for the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan having acquired jurisdiction to receive and investigate administrative complaints against barangay and/or municipal elective officials and thereafter abdicate its power to impose preventive suspension in favor of the Mayor who may or may not concur with the preliminary results of the investigation despite the sanggunian's initial findings of the existence of all the elements which warrant the imposition thereof. In Nera vs. Garcia (106 Phil 1031), the Supreme Court held that a preventive suspension is a preliminary step In an administrative investigation. It may be ordered even before the charges are heard as well as before the official Concerned iS given an opportunity to prove his innocence, being merely a measure that is precisely designed to prevent the accused from hampering the normal course of the Investigation with his influence and authority ovér possible witnesses or to keep him off the records and other evidence and to assist prosecutors in firming up a case, if any, against an erring local official (Lacson vs. Roque, 92 Phil 456; Ganzon vs. Court of Appeals, 200 SCRA 271). Such practice would thus render nugatory the law vesting jurisdiction upon the Sangguniang Bayan or Panlungsoql the power to investigate, hear and decide administrative complaints. (Nera vs. Garcia 106 Phil 1031) It would be inconsistent with the essence of jurisdiction which is the authority to hear and decide a case. Well settled is the rule that statutes are to be construed in the light of the purposes to be achieved and the evils sought to be remedied. We, therefore, have to consider the spirit and reason of the statute wheie a literal meaning would lead to absurdity, contradiction, injustice, or would defeat the clear purpose of the lawmakers. There further exists a valid presumption that undesirable consequences were never intended by a legislative measure and that a construction of which the statute is fairly susceptible is favored to avoid all objectionable, mischievous, indefensible, wrongful, evil and injurious consequences (Ursua vs. Cowt of Appeals, 255 SCRA 147, April 10, 1996). In fine, as to whether or not the power to impose preventive suspension Is a ministerial or discretionary (unction on the part of the governor or mayor, we are of the considered view that the authority or the local chief executives (Governor/Mayor) to impose preventive suspension is purely ministerial since the disciplinary authority over etTing municipal or barangay elective officials is the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Pantungsod or Sangguniang Bayan, as the case may be. Hence, aß:er the sanggunian shall have determined the

-4- necessity to warrant the imposition of preventive suspension, the same must bé implemented by the local chief executive concerned. Moreover, the Court of Appeals ruling in the case of Gov. Francisco T. Matugas, Petitioner versus The Honorable Floripinas C. Buyser, as Judge of Branch 31 Regional Trial Court of Dapar Surigao del Norte and Mayor Alma G. Navarro, Respondents in CA-G.R. SP No. 55563 is instructive where it was held that "the authority to determine whether the evidence warrants the preventive suspension of an elective municipa/ officia/ finds support in the ruling in Espiritu vs. Me/gar that the office or body that is invested with the power of remova/ or suspension should be the sole Judge of the necessity and sufficiency of the cause. Moreover, to give to the prov/nc/a/ governor the authority Io determ/ne whether preventive suspension is warranted on the grounds that the evidence of guilt is strong and given the gravity of the offense, there is great probability that the continuance in office of the tespondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence without prior recommendation by the Sangguniang Pan/a/awigan, would constitute undue inteMerence on the authority of said body to investigate and discipline elective municipal officials and preempt the latter's decision on the administrative case. " As such, please be informed that if the Mayor is being directed by the Sanggunian to implement its order, resolution, decision or judgment issued pursuant to the exercise of its quasi-judicial powers conferred by Section 61 of the Local Government Code, it is the ministerial duty of the Mayor to execute the same and he has no discretion to determine the propriety of the implementation of the order, resolution or judgment or decision. "the service or implementation of the order, resolution or decision has to be made without unnecessary delay so that after being duly informed, the respondent can immediately take steps to ptotect his interests by filing an appeal or apply for other appropriate relief. The refusal of the Municipal Mayor to implement a preventive suspension can be considered as obstruction of justice and therefore would be tantamount to grave misconduct for which he may be administratively sanctioned. Hoping that we have clarified the matter. Very truly yours, SE D. 1.1 DIR. LFöNrco B.
